summary:
Ladakh is a union territory of India and stands under India's national framework as rewritten by the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill, which India's Parliament passed in March 2026. As national law it sets the recognition baseline for a trans visitor in Ladakh, whatever the union territory's own administration does.

The amendment removes the right to self-identification affirmed by the Supreme Court of India's 2014 judgment, limits legal recognition to historically accepted socio-cultural groups such as hijra and kinner and to intersex individuals, and excludes self-identified trans men, trans women and non-binary people who identify outside those categories. It also mandates medical certification for identity recognition. Human Rights Watch described the bill as a major setback that strips thousands of people of rights and increases their risk.

No Ladakh-specific signal on enforcement, documents, facilities or incidents was identified in the source inventory; the national assessment applies.
tangentialFactors: The national framework's recognition scheme is applied uniformly across Indian states and union territories, so a trans visitor's experience in Ladakh will track the national baseline rather than any distinct local policy.
localsOnly: Residents of Ladakh fall under the same national recognition scheme as visitors: legal recognition is limited to historically accepted socio-cultural groups and intersex individuals, with medical certification required, and self-identified trans men, trans women and non-binary people outside those categories are excluded.
outOfScopeNotes: The source inventory contains no Ladakh-specific information on local enforcement practice, identity-document handling at checkpoints or airports within Ladakh, facility access, or incidents affecting trans people in the union territory. Whether Ladakh's administration has issued any implementing instructions under the 2026 amendment is unresolved and not sourced here.
